title: polyjose conformance vector
description: One file under conformance/vectors/ holds exactly one vector. Every platform runner (Rust, WASM, Node, Kotlin, Swift) must reject a file that does not match this schema, and must fail (never skip) a vector whose operation it does not implement. A vector may list in "features" the polyjose cargo features it needs; a runner where one is not enabled reports the vector SKIPPED with the feature names, and never counts it as passing. Operations without an input/expect definition here are reserved for the features that will define them; until then no runner implements them, so a vector using one fails. Bytes under test of the codec operations (b64url.*, jwk.thumbprint) are given in lowercase hex, never base64url, so the codec is not checked against itself. The jws.* and jwe.* operations give octets as canonical base64url (members ending in _b64u), the form JOSE fields natively have; the codec is not under test there. The keys.* operations give keys as PEM text, JWK objects and DER as canonical base64url (der_b64u), never hex. jwks.select gives a JWK Set and a selector as JSON objects and expects the selected key as a JWK object, compared as a JSON value. The jwt.* operations give tokens as text, keys as JWK and JWK Set objects, and the time as integer seconds (now); a runner builds a fixed clock from now and never reads its platform's clock (ADR 0028).

source.description: Where the expected value comes from: an RFC section ("RFC 7638 §3.1"), an upstream suite, or "polyjose" for a project-defined negative vector.

description.description: What the vector checks, in one sentence.

features.description: Optional. The polyjose cargo features the vector needs: fixed-rng (the test-vector RNG feature of ADR 0041 §3; conformance/README.md gives its cargo name) for jwe.encrypt with rng_b64u or protected_b64u, deflate for zip (ADR 0017). A runner whose build lacks one reports the vector SKIPPED, naming the features, and never counts it as passing. No binding enables the test-vector RNG (ADR 0005), so fixed-rng vectors are Rust-only.

hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal, two digits per octet; empty for zero octets.

base64url.description: Characters of the base64url alphabet (RFC 4648 §5), no padding.

count.description: A non-negative integer that an unsigned 32-bit integer holds (ADR 0030 u32), so every binding reads it natively and exactly.

seconds.description: Whole seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, ignoring leap seconds (RFC 7519 §2), within ±(2^53 − 1): the NumericDate and clock range (RFC 7493 §2.2; ADR 0027 §2, ADR 0028 §1), which every binding holds exactly, JavaScript numbers included. Negative values are dates before 1970.

jwe.description: A JWE: a string in the Compact Serialization (RFC 7516 §7.1), or an object in the flattened or general JWE JSON Serialization (RFC 7516 §7.2), which a runner passes to the library as its JSON text. Otherwise unconstrained: malformed JWEs are under test.

jws.description: A JWS: a string in the Compact Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.1), or an object in the flattened or general JWS JSON Serialization (RFC 7515 §7.2), which a runner passes to the library as its JSON text. Otherwise unconstrained: malformed JWSs are under test.

alg_list.description: An algorithm allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1) of names, passed to the library as given: JWS "alg" names for jws.*, JWE "alg" or "enc" names for jwe.*. For jws.*, an empty list, "none" or an unknown name is refused by the library with AlgorithmNotAllowed; for jwe.*, an empty list is AlgorithmNotAllowed, and an unknown or unimplemented name may be listed but never decrypts (UnsupportedAlgorithm, the support check comes first). Vectors may test all of these.

failure.description: The operation must fail with exactly this error code.

b64url_encode_input.description: Octets to encode as unpadded base64url (RFC 7515 §2).

b64url_encode_ok.description: Encoding cannot fail, so only a success expectation exists.

b64url_decode_input.description: Text to decode; any string, since rejected encodings are under test.

jwk_thumbprint_input.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported and then hashed (RFC 7638 §3). Its members are deliberately unconstrained: invalid keys are under test. hash is optional and any string: absent means the core default, SHA-256 (RFC 9278 §5, ADR 0054 §8); exactly sha-256, SHA-256, sha256 and the 384/512 forms are accepted, case-sensitive, and any other name is a vector outcome (UnsupportedAlgorithm, ADR 0054 §8.2), never a schema error.

jwk_thumbprint_ok.description: The base64url JWK Thumbprint (RFC 7638 §3) and its JWK Thumbprint URI (RFC 9278 §3).

jwks_select_input.description: Select one key from a JWK Set (RFC 7517 §5) with a selector (ADR 0054 §1-§2; the binding jwks_select of ADR 0030 §4 as amended by ADR 0054 §9). The runner imports jwks, then builds the selector in the order kid, alg, key_use, then selects; the first error is the outcome (ADR 0054 §4 precedence: set import errors, then UnsupportedAlgorithm from the selector, then NoMatchingKey or MultipleMatchingKeys).

jwks.description: A JWK Set (RFC 7517 §5) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome (a missing or non-array keys is InvalidKey, an RSA private member is UnsupportedAlgorithm, ADR 0021, ADR 0029 §3), and members the import skips (ADR 0041 §2) are under test.

jwks_selector.description: The binding JwkSelector (ADR 0030 §4, ADR 0054 §9): every member optional, {} selecting every member (ADR 0054 §1.3). kid is compared for exact equality (RFC 7517 §4.5). alg and key_use are any string, passed to the library as given: an unsupported alg (none, RSA1_5, RSA-OAEP, an enc name, an unregistered name) or a key_use other than sig or enc is a vector outcome (UnsupportedAlgorithm, ADR 0054 §1.1), never a schema error.

jwks_select_ok.description: The one matching member (ADR 0054 §4) as its core serialization, a JSON object compared as a JSON value (member order ignored). It may hold private members (EC and OKP d, oct k; ADR 0054 §3).

jws_signer.description: One signature to compute: its JWS Protected Header as exact octets (RFC 7515 §5.1 step 3; the runner signs over them verbatim), its JWS Unprotected Header (RFC 7515 §7.2.1), and its key. The runner imports key, then parses protected_b64u, then header; the first error is the outcome.

protected_b64u.description: BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)), kept verbatim for the signing input (e.g. RFC 7515 A.1's CRLF header).

header.description: The JWS Unprotected Header as a JSON object (JSON serializations only). Unconstrained: header errors are under test.

key.description: The signing JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jws_sign_input.description: Sign a payload (RFC 7515 §5.1) in one serialization, with one signer (compact, flattened) or several (general, in order), attached or detached (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

payload_b64u.description: The JWS Payload octets, canonical base64url; the runner decodes them (with b64:false, RFC 7797, the octets themselves are signed).

detached.description: Leave the payload out of the output (RFC 7515 Appendix F).

jws_sign_exact.description: A deterministic signature (HMAC, EdDSA): the exact output. A compact JWS is compared as a string; a JSON JWS is compared as a JSON value, so member order does not matter (RFC 8259 §4) but every octet of every string does.

jws_verify_with.description: The key and allow-list a runner verifies its own randomized output with.

jws_sign_roundtrip.description: A randomized signature (ECDSA): the runner checks that its output has the requested serialization's shape, verifies it with verify_with (passing the payload separately when detached), and checks the verified payload equals payload_b64u. Any failure there fails the vector.

jws_verify_input.description: Verify a JWS (RFC 7515 §5.2) with one key and an allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1), under the processing order of ADR 0026 §2. The runner imports key, then builds the options, then verifies; the first error is the outcome.

key.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

detached_payload_b64u.description: The detached payload (RFC 7515 Appendix F); the JWS then carries none.

max_input_len.description: The largest serialized JWS accepted, in octets (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

max_signatures.description: The most signatures a general JSON JWS may have (ADR 0026 §7); the library default when absent.

jws_verify_ok.description: The verified JWS: its payload, the alg of the signature that verified, and that signature's index (0 for compact and flattened; the first that verifies, in array order, for general, ADR 0026 §3).

jwe_recipient.description: One recipient to encrypt to (RFC 7516 §5.1 steps 1-8). The runner imports key, then parses header; the first error is the outcome.

alg.description: The JWE "alg" (RFC 7516 §4.1.1), passed as given; an unimplemented one is the library's UnsupportedAlgorithm.

key.description: The recipient's JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object: a public key, or the oct key of dir, A*KW, A*GCMKW or the PBES2 password. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

header.description: The JWE Per-Recipient Unprotected Header (RFC 7516 §7.2.1) as a JSON object (JSON serializations only). Unconstrained: header errors are under test.

p2c.description: The PBES2 iteration count (RFC 7518 §4.8.1.2); the library default (10,000, ADR 0023) when absent.

p2s_len.description: The length of the random PBES2 salt input, in octets (RFC 7518 §4.8.1.1); the library default (16) when absent.

jwe_encrypt_input.description: Encrypt a plaintext (RFC 7516 §5.1) in one serialization to one recipient (compact, flattened) or several (general, in order). The runner builds the recipients, then parses protected, then unprotected; the first error is the outcome. With rng_b64u or protected_b64u it calls the library's reproducible encryption (feature fixed-rng, which the vector must list in features).

protected.description: Extra JWE Protected Header parameters (typ, cty, kid, ...) as a JSON object; polyjose sets alg, enc, zip and the key management parameters itself and refuses them here (InvalidHeader).

protected_b64u.description: The exact encoded JWE Protected Header to reproduce (feature fixed-rng): used verbatim for the AAD and the output only if it decodes to a header JSON-equal to the one polyjose builds, else InvalidFormat.

unprotected.description: The JWE Shared Unprotected Header (RFC 7516 §7.2.1) as a JSON object (JSON serializations only).

aad_b64u.description: The JWE AAD octets (RFC 7516 §7.2.1; JSON serializations only).

compress.description: Compress with zip DEF (RFC 7516 §4.1.3; feature deflate, which the vector must list in features).

rng_b64u.description: The octets the encryption draws, in the documented order (CEK, then each recipient's key management, then the content IV; feature fixed-rng). Every octet must be drawn.

jwe_encrypt_exact.description: A reproducible encryption's exact output (rng_b64u given): a compact JWE is compared as a string; a JSON JWE is compared as a JSON value, so member order does not matter (RFC 8259 §4) but every octet of every string does.

jwe_decrypt_with.description: The key and allow-lists a runner decrypts its own randomized output with.

jwe_encrypt_roundtrip.description: A randomized encryption (OS CSPRNG): the runner checks that its output has the requested serialization's shape, decrypts it with decrypt_with, and checks the plaintext equals plaintext_b64u. Any failure there fails the vector.

jwe_decrypt_input.description: Decrypt a JWE (RFC 7516 §5.2) with one key and the allow-lists (RFC 8725 §3.1), under the plan's error order (ADR 0026 §2 applied to JWE). The runner imports key, then builds the policy, then decrypts; the first error is the outcome.

key.description: A JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object, imported with the library's JWK import. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

understood_crit.description: The crit extension names the caller understands (RFC 7516 §4.1.13); none when absent.

max_input_len.description: The largest serialized JWE accepted, in octets (ADR 0026 §7); the library default (1 MiB) when absent.

max_recipients.description: The most recipients a JSON JWE may have (ADR 0026 §7); the library default (16) when absent.

max_pbes2_count.description: The largest PBES2 p2c accepted (ADR 0023); the library default (10,000) when absent.

max_decompressed_len.description: The largest inflated plaintext (ADR 0017); the library default (250,000) when absent.

jwe_decrypt_ok.description: The decrypted JWE: its plaintext, and the index of the recipient that decrypted (0 for compact and flattened; the first that decrypts, in array order, for general).

keys_import_pem_input.description: Import one RFC 7468 PEM block with the library's PEM key import (ADR 0018 §3): the label selects the structure (PRIVATE KEY: PKCS#8, RFC 5958 §2; PUBLIC KEY: SPKI, RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7; EC PRIVATE KEY: SEC1, RFC 5915 §3; RSA PUBLIC KEY: PKCS#1, RFC 8017 App. A.1.1). Any string, since rejected encodings are under test.

keys_import_pem_ok.description: The imported key as a JWK (RFC 7517 §4), compared as a JSON value: member order is ignored (RFC 8259 §4), every string must match exactly. An imported key never has kty oct and carries no alg.

keys_export_pem_input.description: Export a JWK as one RFC 7468 PEM block in format (ADR 0018 §3). The runner imports jwk with the library's JWK import first; an import error is the vector's outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_export_pem_ok.description: The exact PEM text: 64-character lines, LF line endings and a final newline, in OpenSSL 4's DER layout (ADR 0018 §3); compared as a string.

keys_import_der_input.description: Import DER in the structure format names, with the library's DER key import (ADR 0018 §3); there is no format sniffing (ADR 0007), and DER of another structure fails. The runner decodes der_b64u (canonical base64url); a value that does not decode canonically is a broken vector, never an outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_import_der_ok.description: The imported key as a JWK (RFC 7517 §4), compared as a JSON value: member order is ignored (RFC 8259 §4), every string must match exactly. An imported key never has kty oct and carries no alg.

keys_export_der_input.description: Export a JWK as DER in format (ADR 0018 §3), with the format matrix of keys.export_pem. The runner imports jwk with the library's JWK import first; an import error is the vector's outcome.

format.description: pkcs8 (RFC 5958 §2), sec1 (RFC 5915 §3), spki (RFC 5280 §4.1.2.7) or pkcs1 (RFC 8017 App. A.1.1, RSA public keys).

keys_export_der_ok.description: The exact DER, in OpenSSL 4's layout (ADR 0018 §3), as canonical base64url; compared as a string.

keys_generate_for_input.description: Generate a private key for an algorithm with the library's generate_for (ADR 0018 §5) from the OS CSPRNG. alg is a JWS alg, a JWE alg or a JWE enc name, resolved in the one registry of RFC 7518 §7.1 (names unique and case-sensitive); any string, since unknown names are under test.

keys_generated_shape.description: What a generated key is, without its random material: kty, crv (EC and OKP only), the alg the key is bound to (RFC 7517 §4.4) and the length of k in octets (oct only). Compared as a JSON value, so a member the generated key has and the shape omits fails too.

keys_generate_for_ok.description: Generated keys are random, so only their shape is expected. The runner also checks that the key is private, has exactly the members RFC 7518 §6.2.1-§6.2.2 (EC), RFC 8037 §2 (OKP) or RFC 7518 §6.4.1 (oct) define plus alg, and imports back unchanged; any failure there fails the vector.

jwt_typ.description: How the JWS Protected Header's typ is checked (RFC 7515 §4.1.9, RFC 8725 §3.11-§3.12; ADR 0027 §5): default accepts typ absent or JWT; exact requires typ present and equal to value as a media type; any skips the check. value is required with exact and allowed with nothing else.

jwt_policy.description: The JWT validation policy (RFC 7519 §4.1, §7.2; RFC 8725 §3; ADR 0027 §3-§5, ADR 0029 §4). Every member is optional; an absent member keeps the library default (exp required, leeway 60 s, no issuer, subject or audience accepted, typ mode default, 8 key candidates), which a runner never restates. A boolean member set to false is the same as absent.

issuer.description: The accepted issuer, or a list of them (RFC 7519 §4.1.1, RFC 8725 §3.8): iss must equal one exactly.

audience.description: The accepted audiences (RFC 7519 §4.1.3, RFC 8725 §3.9): aud must contain one. Without it a token carrying aud is rejected (ADR 0027 §4).

subject.description: The expected subject (RFC 7519 §4.1.2): sub must equal it.

leeway.description: The clock skew allowed on exp, nbf and iat, in whole seconds (RFC 7519 §4.1.4-§4.1.5). The library refuses more than 600 with InvalidClaim (ADR 0027 §3).

max_age.description: The largest age of iat in seconds; makes iat required (RFC 7519 §4.1.6, ADR 0027 §3).

require.description: Claim names that must be present, with any value (RFC 7519 §4, ADR 0027 §4).

allow_missing_exp.description: true accepts a token without exp: the explicit opt-out of ADR 0007's required exp (ADR 0027 §3).

ignore_audience.description: true accepts a token carrying aud when no audience is configured: the explicit opt-out of RFC 7519 §4.1.3 (ADR 0027 §4, RFC 8725 §3.9).

profile.description: access_token: validate a JWT access token (RFC 9068 §4): typ at+jwt, the RFC 9068 §2.2 claims, with issuer and audience required (the library refuses the policy without them, InvalidClaim). typ mode default contradicts it and is a broken vector.

max_key_candidates.description: The most JWK Set members tried for one token; more candidates is NoMatchingKey (ADR 0029 §4).

jwt_decrypt.description: The outer JWE layer of a nested JWT (RFC 7519 §5.2, §7.2 step 8; RFC 8725 §3.3; ADR 0027 §7): the decrypting JWK and both allow-lists, as jwe.decrypt takes them, and the PBES2 bound (ADR 0023; the library default 10,000 when absent).

key.description: The decrypting JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jwt_validate_input.description: Validate a JWT (RFC 7519 §7.2) at the time now, with an allow-list (RFC 8725 §3.1) and exactly one of key or jwks (ADR 0029 §1); with decrypt, as a nested JWT (ADR 0027 §7). The runner builds a fixed clock from now and never reads its platform's clock (ADR 0028 §4). It imports decrypt.key, then builds decrypt's lists, then imports key or jwks, then builds the policy, then validates; the first error is the outcome.

token.description: The token as given, any string: malformed tokens are under test.

key.description: One verification JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jwks.description: A JWK Set (RFC 7517 §5) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome (an RSA private member is UnsupportedAlgorithm, ADR 0021, ADR 0029 §3).

jwt_validate_ok.description: The validated JWT: its Claims Set, compared as a JSON value (member order ignored, numbers compared as doubles); the alg that verified; and key_index, the zero-based position in the JWK Set of the member that verified (ADR 0029 §4), present exactly when the input has jwks.

jwt_issue_validate.description: How the runner validates the token a jwt.issue vector issued: the jwt_validate_input members other than token, with the same rules (exactly one of key or jwks).

key.description: One verification JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object.

jwks.description: A JWK Set (RFC 7517 §5) as a JSON object.

jwt_encrypt.description: The JWE layer of a nested JWT to issue (RFC 7519 §7.1 step 5, §11.2; ADR 0027 §7): one recipient's key management alg and JWK (a public key, or an oct key), and the content encryption enc, each passed as given. polyjose puts cty JWT in the protected header itself.

key.description: The recipient's JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

jwt_issue_input.description: Issue a JWT (RFC 7519 §7.1): sign claims with alg and key (ADR 0027 §8), then, with encrypt, encrypt the signed JWT as a nested JWT (ADR 0027 §7). The runner imports key, then parses claims, then imports encrypt.key, then signs, then encrypts; the first error is the outcome. With validate, it validates what it issued. RS* and PS* issuing is UnsupportedAlgorithm (ADR 0021).

claims.description: The JWT Claims Set (RFC 7519 §4) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: claim errors are under test.

alg.description: The JWS alg (RFC 7515 §4.1.1), passed as given.

key.description: The signing JWK (RFC 7517 §4) as a JSON object. Unconstrained: an import error is the vector's outcome.

typ.description: The header typ (RFC 7519 §5.1): absent for the library default (JWT), a string to set it (for example at+jwt), null to omit it.

jwt_issue_exact.description: A deterministic signed JWT (HMAC, EdDSA): the exact compact token, compared as a string. Not with encrypt, whose output is randomized. With validate, the runner also validates it.

jwt_issue_validated.description: A token the runner checks itself: it must be a compact JWS (three parts) or, with encrypt, a compact JWE (five), and with validate it must validate, with the issued alg and claims. validate is required unless encrypt is given (an RSA-OAEP-256 recipient cannot be decrypted, ADR 0021).
